ra: Zeus-Oromasdes is the supreme deity of the Commagenian dynastic pantheon at Nemrud Dag.
Apollo-Mithras-Helios-Hermes is one of the seated colossal deities of the Commagenian pantheon.
Artagnes-Heracles-Ares is one of the seated colossal deities of the Commagenian pantheon.
The Tyche of Commagene is seated among the divine colossi of the pantheon at Nemrud Dag.
Antiochus I Theos enthroned himself as a deified king among the gods of his own dynastic pantheon.
Ancient interpretatio: the theonym Zeus-Oromasdes explicitly equates the Commagenian supreme god with Greek Zeus.
Ancient interpretatio: Oromasdes is the Hellenized form of Iranian Ahura Mazda, fused with Zeus in the Commagenian theonym.
Ancient interpretatio: the composite theonym explicitly identifies the Commagenian solar god with Greek Apollo.
Ancient interpretatio: the Mithras element of the composite theonym derives from Iranian Mithra of the Zoroastrian tradition.
The Commagenian Apollo-Mithras-Helios-Hermes is a key early attestation of the Mithras whose cult later developed in the Roman world.
Ancient interpretatio: the Helios element of the composite theonym identifies the god with the Greek sun god.
Ancient interpretatio: the Hermes element of the composite theonym identifies the god with the Greek messenger god.
Ancient interpretatio: Artagnes is the Hellenized form of Iranian Verethragna, the Zoroastrian yazata of victory.
Ancient interpretatio: the composite theonym explicitly identifies the Commagenian warrior god with Greek Heracles.
Ancient interpretatio: the Ares element of the composite theonym identifies the god with the Greek war god.
The Tyche of Commagene is a regional civic/territorial cult form of the Greek goddess Tyche (Fortune).
The Nemrud Dag dexiosis reliefs depict Antiochus I clasping the hand of Zeus-Oromasdes, asserting his divine legitimacy.
A Nemrud Dag dexiosis relief shows Antiochus I clasping the hand of Artagnes-Heracles-Ares.
